title: Order placement against an inventory store interface
name: Order reservation service

defect.snippet: const reserved = res as Extract<ReserveResult, { status: "reserved" }>;

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how OrderPlacementService consumes the results returned by InventoryStore.reserve? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: ReserveResult has three variants, but placeOrder only handles "insufficient" and then casts everything else to the "reserved" variant. When PgInventoryStore returns { status: "unknown_sku" }, the cast silences the compiler, reserved.reservationId is undefined, undefined is pushed into reservationIds, and the order is inserted with a line for a SKU that does not exist and no stock reserved. A switch on res.status (or an explicit check for "reserved" with an exhaustive never default) would make the compiler force handling of every variant.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The second of three order lines gets { status: "insufficient" } from reserve. What happens to the reservation made for the first line?
choices: It stays reserved until a background job expires it
It is released in the catch block before the InsufficientStockError is rethrown
It is released only if the orders.insert call fails
It is converted into a backorder for the same order ref
choiceQuestions.explanation: The InsufficientStockError is thrown inside the try, so the catch calls releaseAll(reservationIds), which holds the first line's id, then rethrows. Nothing in the code expires reservations, releases only on insert failure, or creates backorders.

choiceQuestions.prompt: If inventory.release throws for one reservation id during cleanup, what does the caller of placeOrder observe?
choices: The release error replaces the original error
placeOrder returns the order ref anyway
The original error that triggered cleanup, after the remaining releases are still attempted
choiceQuestions.explanation: releaseAll catches and logs each release failure and continues the loop, so the catch in placeOrder then rethrows the original err. The release error is never thrown, no ref is returned on the failure path, and no AggregateError is built.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the InventoryStore interface return a ReserveResult union for insufficient stock instead of PgInventoryStore throwing InsufficientStockError itself?
choices: Expected business outcomes become typed values the caller must inspect, while thrown errors are reserved for infrastructure failures
Throwing from inside a pg transaction would leave the row lock held forever
TypeScript cannot type-check thrown errors, so unions are faster at runtime
It lets PgInventoryStore avoid the ROLLBACK on that path
choiceQuestions.explanation: The union makes stock shortages and unknown SKUs part of the method's typed contract, separate from database exceptions which still propagate via throw. PgInventoryStore's catch would roll back and release the lock on a throw too; performance is not the reason; and the insufficient path does still ROLLBACK.
